language.script_notes: Vietnamese is the giveaway: Latin script but with the densest diacritics of any language — stacked tone marks over vowels, plus the barred letter đ and vowels ơ ư ă â ê ô. That alone separates Vietnam from Laos, Cambodia, Thailand and China. Small red national flags are often flown outside houses and shops. .vn domain.

road_furniture.bollard_shape: Concrete post; exact profile not confirmed — verify against photos.
road_furniture.guardrail_type: Standard steel W-beam on highways; many rural roads have none.
road_furniture.line_paint: White and yellow centre lines where roads are marked; not diagnostic. Sign support poles are often painted in red-and-white stripes.
road_furniture.curb_style: Kerbs in towns are frequently painted, usually black-and-white.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: Concrete utility poles, and their markings vary by regional power company — a genuine North/Central/South tell (see the regional profiles). Yellow-topped concrete kilometre stones on national highways.

architecture.roof_style: Dominated by the narrow street frontage of 'tube houses' rather than a roof shape; corrugated metal and flat concrete roofs behind.
architecture.roof_material: Corrugated metal, concrete slab, some clay tile.
architecture.wall_construction: Masonry 'tube houses' (nhà ống) — tall, very narrow (often only 3–4 m wide), several storeys, with ornate and colourful street facades.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Bright pastels and saturated colours; mustard-yellow on French colonial buildings.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Tube houses everywhere; mustard-yellow French colonial villas and shophouses with shutters in Hanoi and Saigon; communist propaganda billboards; Buddhist and Cao Đài temples.

nature.vegetation: Wet rice paddies almost everywhere in the lowlands; palms; tropical broadleaf forest in the hills; coffee in the Central Highlands and rubber plantations inland.
nature.terrain: Two big rice deltas — the Red River in the north, the Mekong in the south — joined by a long narrow coastal strip, with a mountainous interior and sharply pointed limestone karst in the north and centre.
nature.climate_signature: The north has a cool, often grey and drizzly winter (down toward 10–15 °C); the centre and south are hot and humid year-round. A bare, overcast look points north.

vehicles.plate_color: White with black text on private vehicles; yellow with black text on commercial vehicles (taxis, trucks, ride-hail — since 2020); blue on government vehicles; red on military.
vehicles.plate_format: DDLL-NNN.NN — the first two digits are a province code (29–33 Hanoi, 50–59 Ho Chi Minh City).
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Dense swarms of motorbikes and scooters are the single strongest Vietnam signal.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Older generations; Vietnam has no current official car coverage and is treated as a 'legacy' country in GeoGuessr.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Much of the coverage is moped-mounted — you can often see handlebars, a wing mirror and the driver's helmet in shot — plus a lot of trekker footage. Imagery tends to look older and lower quality than neighbouring countries.

confusion_set.shared_traits: South-East Asian Buddhist context, rice paddies, right-hand traffic, similar road furniture
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Vietnamese is heavily-accented Latin script; Lao is its own rounded abugida. Vietnam is far more developed and densely built, with motorbike swarms and tube houses.

confusion_set.shared_traits: The Mekong delta and lowland rice country continue across the border; similar climate and temples
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Khmer script vs Vietnamese Latin script. Cambodia is flatter, poorer-looking and less densely built than southern Vietnam.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Red-and-white infrastructure, karst scenery in the north, communist iconography, dense motorbike use near the border
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Chinese Hanzi signage vs Vietnamese Latin script; Chinese plates and road design differ; China drives on the right too, so lean on the writing.
